display.title: Episode 209: The Lost Letter, Conclusion (Tu B'Shvat)
display.summary_short: A Tu B'Shvat lesson on people as trees whose fruits are good deeds, Shema with a young guest, the ending of 'The Lost Letter', and Mitzvah Time on stacking holy books.
display.summary_long: Broadcast the week of Tu B'Shvat 5746, which fell on Shabbos. Uncle Yossi explains that the Mishnah lists several 'Rosh Hashanahs', including the New Year for trees on the fifteenth of Shevat. We eat the fruits for which the Torah praises Eretz Yisroel, say Borei Pri Ha'etz and Shehecheyanu on a new fruit, and learn from the tree: a person is like a tree of the field, and our fruits are our mitzvos and good deeds. After the Hakochainik march and the Shema with a young guest, 'The Lost Letter' concludes. Leibel, now poor, travels to the wealthy Reb Shalom, insists on handing him the Baal Shem Tov's letter in person, and is let in. Reb Shalom recognizes his teacher's seal and weeps as he reads it aloud: Leibel failed to value a blessing and has paid for it, and Reb Shalom must now set him back on his feet. The letter is dated that very day. In Mitzvah Time, Uncle Yossi teaches that no sefer may be placed on top of a Chumash, while Nevi'im and Kesuvim are equal to each other. The show closes with Tu B'Shvat wishes.
display.lesson: Value every blessing, especially a tzaddik's; and like a tree, a person is known by the fruits of his good deeds.

date.note: 'This coming Shabbos Kodesh is the fifteenth of Shevat' (Tu B'Shvat 5746 = Saturday 25 Jan 1986); the Tuesday before is 21 Jan, matching the weekly estimate.
